title: EU consumer authorities converted ticket-resale concerns into platform commitments on identity, price, pressure, ranking, and remedy
source_unit: European Commission Consumer Protection Cooperation Network dialogue with Viagogo
geography: European Union and European Economic Area consumer-facing Viagogo websites

observations.period: 16 May 2024 commitments; implementation deadlines through 31 August 2024

denominator.unit: EU/EEA consumers using Viagogo ticket-resale websites; no affected-consumer count disclosed

seller_identity.value: Viagogo committed to identify whether a seller is a trader or private person and display relevant trader details

marketplace_role.value: Viagogo committed to make its status as a secondary marketplace visibly clear

legal_jurisdiction.value: EU consumers would be able to bring legal actions in their Member State of residence and retain mandatory local-law protections

mechanism.value: In secondary cultural markets, consumer agency depends on knowing who sells the ticket and which legal protections remain available, not only on seeing a nominal ticket price

observations.method: European Commission factsheet summarizing commitments made by Viagogo following dialogue with the CPC Network and national consumer authorities.
observations.uncertainty: The commitments document planned or implemented changes but do not quantify prior consumer harm, actual compliance across every EU/EEA site, or successful use of legal remedies.
observations.subgroup: Consumers purchasing or attempting to purchase resale tickets on Viagogo sites directed to EU/EEA consumers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Disclosure of seller identity and jurisdiction may improve formal rights without changing scarcity, resale markups, affordability, or consumers' practical ability to litigate.

observations.period: 16 May 2024 commitments; price, ranking, and pressure controls

denominator.unit: EU/EEA Viagogo ticket listings and checkout journeys; no listing or consumer count disclosed

price_display.value: Viagogo committed to consistent fee terminology and clearer display of estimated tax, booking fees, and delivery-fee conditions near ticket prices

seat_information.value: Viagogo committed to display seat numbers when sellers provide them

ranking_explanation.value: Viagogo committed to explain ranking criteria and improve the clarity of its best-value filter

countdown_pressure.value: Viagogo committed to substantially reduce countdown messages and clarify availability and popularity statements

mechanism.value: Ticket resale converts platform interface design into cultural-consumer pressure through incomplete price, ranking opacity, seat uncertainty, and scarcity messaging

observations.method: European Commission factsheet listing CPC concerns and Viagogo website commitments with implementation deadlines.
observations.uncertainty: The factsheet does not measure whether users read or understood the new information, whether pressure messages changed conversion, or whether transparent pricing reduced final prices.
observations.subgroup: EU/EEA consumers comparing resale ticket listings and progressing through Viagogo checkout.
observations.counterinterpretation: More information can increase cognitive load and does not eliminate scarcity or high prices; fewer countdowns may not remove other urgency cues or algorithmic ranking effects.

observations.period: 16 May 2024 commitments; failed, invalid, changed, or cancelled ticket remedy

denominator.unit: EU/EEA Viagogo consumers; no affected-customer count disclosed

refund_window.value: Viagogo committed to allow consumers more time to apply for a refund under its Guarantee when tickets fail

fraud_and_cancelled_events.value: Viagogo committed to continue efforts to remove fraudulent ticket listings and cancelled events quickly

contact_route.value: Viagogo committed to make consumer and authority contact channels more prominent and available for queries and regulatory issues

terms_changes.value: Viagogo committed to advance notice and free cancellation opportunity for future unilateral changes to terms

mechanism.value: The value of a ticketing platform is realized only if failed delivery, invalidity, cancellation, changed terms, and seat substitution have a reachable remedy route

observations.method: European Commission factsheet summary of CPC concerns and Viagogo commitments on guarantees, contact, ticket fraud, cancellations, and terms.
observations.uncertainty: The commitments do not report refund claims, successful resolutions, average time to remedy, or verified compliance after implementation.
observations.subgroup: EU/EEA consumers whose resale tickets are undelivered, invalid, affected by cancellation, or subject to changed platform terms.
observations.counterinterpretation: A formal Guarantee or contact address may remain practically weak if consumers cannot document the problem, meet deadlines, or obtain a response; the factsheet does not test usability.

related_sources.claim: The Commission says the CPC Network will actively monitor implementation, while noting Viagogo did not commit to disclose possible delivery-fee amounts at the beginning when multiple delivery options exist or clearly explain additional rights against the actual seller or event organizer after cancellation or postponement.
The European Commission's coordinated-actions page places the Viagogo dialogue within EU marketplace and digital-services consumer enforcement.
The UK StubHub case supplies a cross-jurisdiction comparator involving hidden fees, automatic refunds, and a financial penalty.

boundary: This record adds an EU/EEA ticket-resale platform-governance episode linking seller identity, price clarity, ranking, scarcity pressure, fraud/cancellation, legal jurisdiction, and remedy routes. It does not quantify affected consumers, verify implementation or compliance, estimate ticket affordability, or prove that the commitments changed cultural participation.
